Transcriptome analysis showed that SlVTE3(2) affected multiple ripening-related pathways, including ethylene biosynthesis and signaling, carotenoid metabolism, and cell wall modification. Although SlVTE3(2) significantly altered the tocopherol composition in tomato fruits, exogenous tocopherol treatment did not affect ripening initiation. These findings provide new insights into the regulation of tomato fruit ripening by the metabolic enzymes.

title: The Transcription Factor StStop1-3 Activates StALMT10 Expression to Enhance Aluminum Tolerance by Promoting Malate Secretion in Potato (Solanum tuberosum L.).
authors: Zhang, Feng; Gou, Huaijuan; Yuan, Anping; Chu, Moli; Zhang, Haiyan; An, Yanlin
journal: Journal of agricultural and food chemistry
abstract: Acidic soils, occupying roughly one-third of arable land, restrict root growth through soluble Al3+ below pH 5.5. Malate exudation chelates Al3+ in the rhizosphere and confers Al tolerance, yet its transcriptional control in potato remains uncharacterized. Here, StSTOP1-3 was identified as a direct activator of the malate transporter gene StALMT10. StALMT10 was root-predominant, encoded a plasma-membrane protein enriched in root tips, and its CRISPR/Cas9 knockout caused Al3+ hypersensitivity, root-tip Al accumulation, and reduced malate exudation. Among three potato STOP1 paralogs, only StSTOP1-3 was rapidly induced by Al3+ and localized to the nucleus. Yeast one-hybrid, dual-luciferase, and DNA pull-down assays confirmed that StSTOP1-3 binds the StALMT10 promoter and activates its transcription. StSTOP1-3 knockout lines showed an even stronger malate-secretion defect than StALMT10 mutants, implying additional downstream targets. Thus, the StSTOP1-3-StALMT10 module confers Al tolerance through root malate secretion, supporting marker-assisted breeding on acidic soils.

title: Structural Modifications Redirect Phenylpyrazole Ectoparasiticides from the Ion Channel Pore to an Allosteric Site on GABA Receptors.
authors: Zhou, Tianhao; Cheng, Zihan; Xie, Honglei; Liu, Ailing; Li, Shoujun; Qiao, Xiaomu; Huang, Jia
journal: Journal of agricultural and food chemistry
abstract: Phenylpyrazole ectoparasiticides, exemplified by fipronil, act as noncompetitive antagonists of arthropod GABA receptors by blocking the ion channel pore. Here, we investigated the molecular mechanism of the newer phenylpyrazole nicofluprole using Drosophila melanogaster. CRISPR/Cas9-mediated mutagenesis and pharmacological assays showed that A301 substitutions in the pore-forming TM2 helix conferred strong resistance to fipronil but had little effect on nicofluprole sensitivity. In contrast, G335 mutations in TM3 markedly reduced nicofluprole activity. Molecular docking supported these findings, indicating that nicofluprole binds at the transmembrane subunit interface rather than within the central pore, consistent with allosteric modulation. These results demonstrate that structural modification of the phenylpyrazole scaffold can redirect target-site engagement from the pore to an allosteric site, explaining the lack of cross-resistance with traditional pore blockers and expanding strategies for GABA receptor-targeted insecticide design.

title: Rotary Piston Valve with Surface-Engraved Microfluidic Channels for Cassette-Based Nucleic Acid Detection.
authors: Cai, Yanwei; Zi, Longbin; Zheng, Jintao; Tang, Yunyan; Wei, Lanlan; Wang, Dou; Jiang, Xingyu
abstract: Point-of-care testing (POCT) plays a crucial role in both clinical- and home-based diagnostics. Integrated POCT systems that combine nucleic acid extraction with detection provide significant advantages, including portable operation, rapid processing, and high sensitivity. In this work, we present a fully automated and integrated nucleic acid detection system based on microfluidic chips with a surface-engraved rotary piston (SERP), which incorporates all of the liquid channels on the surface of one valve. This design consists of only three parts: the chip, the rubber sealing ring, and the rotary valve containing microfluidic channels, allowing the sequential connection of reaction chambers to facilitate nucleic acid extraction, recombinase polymerase amplification (RPA), and clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeats (CRISPR) into a single chip. Our chip consists of only three components, can be fabricated directly by 3D printing, and features a simple structure with a compact size. This platform was employed for the detection of human papillomavirus (HPV16) DNA, achieving a limit of detection (LOD) as low as 60 copies/mL. This result underscores the potential of the SERP as a rapid, cost-effective, and modular solution for POCT applications.

title: An XNA-CRISPR Platform for PAM-Free Detection of the katG Ser315Thr Mutation Associated with Isoniazid Resistance in Tuberculosis.
authors: Liao, Xinyi; Chen, Junhong; Wan, Yunzhu; Xu, Wenfei; Zhou, Jianhua; Liu, Yanping; Li, Xuhui; Yang, Chongguang; Wang, Jiasi
abstract: Drug-resistance Tuberculosis (TB) is a major threat to global public health. Simple and precise detection of the mutations associated with drug resistance is still a significant challenge. CRISPR-based nucleic acid detection has emerged as a transformative technology in molecular diagnostics due to its high specificity and programmability. However, the CRISPR-Cas12a system requires a protospacer adjacent motif (PAM) in the target double-stranded DNA (dsDNA) for efficient recognition and activation, which limits its application for detecting single-nucleotide variants (SNVs). To overcome this limitation, we leveraged high-affinity xenonucleic acids (XNAs) to engineer an XNA-CRISPR platform that combines a helicase and sequence-specific XNAs (such as peptide nucleic acid (PNA), locked nucleic acid (LNA), or 2'-modified RNA), to unwind the dsDNA, enabling them to invade and form stable hybrids, thereby displacing a single strand for PAM-independent Cas12a activation. This recognition mechanism, combining XNA hybridization and CRISPR verification, achieves single-base resolution. To bridge the sensitivity gap for clinical application, we integrated this platform with polydisperse droplet digital technology (PddXNA-CRISPR), which significantly enhanced the sensitivity. Clinical sputum samples were detected by using PddXNA-CRISPR for Mycobacterium tuberculosis (MTB) katG Ser315Thr mutation, which showed 90% concordance with sequencing results. This modular, amplification-free platform expands the CRISPR-based diagnostic toolkit and provides a versatile and sensitive approach for detecting critical SNVs.

title: Spider-Inspired S-Loop Amplification Repurposes an Electron Cage for Photoelectrochemical-Fluorescence Detection of Perfluorooctanoic Acid.
authors: Zheng, Yiwei; Huang, Jingli; Zhang, Xinyue; Li, Xu; Feng, Na; Lu, Wenjie; Wei, Ruxia; Tan, Xuecai; Huang, Kejing; Wu, Jiawen
abstract: Per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances require analytical methods that combine sensitivity with internal result checking. Here, we report an S-Loop CRISPR dual-mode assay (SCDA) for perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA). PFOA-induced aptamer displacement initiates an AMPLON-derived isothermal S-Loop reaction mediated by an eight-arm poly(ethylene glycol) spider-inspired primer (SP), and the resulting amplicons activate Cas12a trans-cleavage. A FAM-quencher reporter provides the fluorescence (FL) output, whereas cleavage-induced removal of CdS from a CdS/gold nanoparticle/ZnIn2S4 photoelectrode releases an electron cage produced by type-I carrier confinement and visible-light shielding of the underlying photoactive layer, thereby restoring the photoelectrochemical (PEC) signal. At target concentrations of 10-13, 10-10, and 10-7 M, Cas12a reporter cleavage was linear with time over the first 10 min, and PEG20000-SP produced the largest amplification response and highest apparent reporter-signal rising rate. PEC and FL calibrations were linear over 10-15-10-7 and 10-14-10-7 M, respectively, with equations I = 12.3328 + 0.7207 log10C (R2 = 0.9929) and F = 13631.32 + 845.64 log10C (R2 = 0.9926). Estimated blank-based limits of detection were 1.27 x 10-16 M (PEC) and 8.34 x 10-16 M (FL); these estimates are below the lowest tested standards and do not establish quantitation below the calibration ranges. Paired results were compared within the common calibration range using log-concentration differences and relative percent differences. Consensus recoveries were 94.3-103.6% in milk and 95.7-103.0% in river water. SCDA therefore combines sensitive dual-readout with an explicit preliminary screen for discordant measurements.

title: Machine Learning-Assisted Multiplexed and Ultrasensitive Biosensing of Pathogenic Bacteria based on a TtAgo-Powered Autocatalytic Nucleic Acid Circuit and Encoded SERS Tags.
authors: Zhang, Xiru; Qiu, Manyan; Huang, Jiaxin; Zhang, Yiyi; Tian, Yuhang; Zhang, Wei; Jiang, Yujun; Zhang, Xianlong
abstract: Programmable nucleases have obtained widespread application in the field of pathogen detection, yet they face considerable challenges in multiplex detection. As a sister technology to CRISPR/Cas systems, Argonaute proteins (Ago) possess programmability, sequence specificity, and multi-turnover capability, rendering them promising candidates for next-generation multiplex detection technologies. Herein, a novel machine learning-assisted amplification-free and multiple SERS biosensing platform based on an Ago-driven autocatalytic nucleic acid circuit (SAANC) was developed for the multiplexed detection of pathogenic bacteria. The SAANC platform utilized the cross-catalytic activity of TtAgo to construct an autocatalytic nucleic acid circuit, enabling continuous reactions without pre-amplification and achieving autocatalytic signal amplification. Meanwhile, by precisely modulating the density of reporter DNA on the surface of silver@Raman reporter@gold nanoparticles (Ag@Ra@Au NPs), both cleavage efficiency and Raman response were significantly enhanced. This integrated approach significantly enhanced reaction efficiency, achieving highly sensitive and specific multiplex detection of pathogenic bacteria. The SAANC method exhibited linear detection ranges of 102-108 CFU/mL for Salmonella typhimurium and 103-108 CFU/mL for Staphylococcus aureus, respectively. Moreover, satisfactory recoveries (89%-110%) in food sample detection were obtained. Furthermore, machine learning-assisted quantitative analysis was introduced to effectively address the challenge of overlapping SERS signals from dual targets, substantially improving the robustness of simultaneous multi-target quantification. This platform provides a feasible strategy for developing high-performance Ago-based multiplex pathogen detection systems and offers an innovative solution for efficient multiplex detection of pathogenic bacteria.

title: Engineering the Metabolic Pathway of Escherichia coli for Efficient Biosynthesis of Lacto-N-tetraose.
authors: Hu, Miaomiao; Qin, Shufang; Zhang, Yilu; Zhang, Tiehua; Zhang, Tao
journal: Journal of agricultural and food chemistry
abstract: Lacto-N-tetraose (LNT), a core component of human milk oligosaccharides (HMOs), plays essential biological roles; however, its production remains challenging due to low conversion efficiency and the accumulation of intermediates. In this study, a systematic metabolic engineering strategy was applied to Escherichia coli BL21(DE3) to enhance LNT production. Key approaches included CRISPR-Cas9-mediated host optimization, chromosomal integration of critical pathway genes, and systematic optimization of fermentation conditions. As a result, the engineered strain achieved an LNT titer of 36.29 g/L, with a molar conversion rate of 95.6% from the intermediate lacto-N-triose II to LNT, representing the highest conversion efficiency reported to date for LNT biosynthesis in a single microbial strain. This integrated strategy significantly improves production efficiency while reducing the burden of downstream purification, providing a robust technological framework for the industrial biosynthesis of LNT and other high-value oligosaccharides.

title: DNA Fragment Fusion-Triggered Label-Free Detection of Listeria monocytogenes Subtypes via Fusion RAA and Hybrid Split G-Quadruplex.
authors: Li, Fan; Han, Rui; Yao, Ruiting; Zhou, Baoqing; Jiang, Xinxin; Zhu, Haorui; Shi, Yiheng; Fan, Lihua; Wu, Di; Li, Guoliang
journal: Journal of agricultural and food chemistry
abstract: Bacterial subtype detection using multiplex amplification with multiple distinguishable labels is complex and costly, whereas recombinant DNA technology via fragment fusion provides a simpler, cheaper alternative. Here, we propose a label-free method for Listeria monocytogenes subtype detection based on a hybrid split G-quadruplex (G4) and fusion recombinase-aided amplification (RAA)-cascaded CRISPR/Cas13a (HGFRC) platform. Fusion RAA co-amplified species-specific and clonal complex (CC)-specific targets into 535 bp fusion products, which activated T7 transcription and Cas13a trans-cleavage activity. Activated Cas13a cleaved the RNA linker, disrupting G4 assembly and reducing fluorescence to generate a signal-off response. This design eliminated labeled probes, enabling single-signal detection. The assay achieved a sensitivity of 1.0 x 101 CFU/mL within 45 min, with good specificity and sample suitability. Overall, this study provides a label-free, sensitive, and specific method for detecting L. monocytogenes CC5, offering new insights for bacterial subtype biosensing.

title: HMGB1 and HMGB2 Are O4-Alkylthymidine-Binding Proteins.
authors: He, Xiaomei; Liang, Xiaochen; Wang, Pengcheng; Chen, Junmin; Wang, Yinsheng
abstract: Exposure to endogenous and exogenous sources of alkylating agents leads to DNA lesions that can impair cell survival and confer genome instability by eliciting mutations during DNA replication and transcription. Among the DNA alkylation adducts, O4-alkylthymidine (O4-alkyldT) lesions are poorly repaired in mammalian cells, and not much is known about the cellular proteins involved in the recognition of these lesions. Here, we found that HMGB1 and HMGB2 bind directly and preferentially to O4-alkyldT-containing DNA. CRISPR-Cas9-mediated ablation of HMGB1 or HMGB2 led to an attenuated level of transcriptional bypass of these lesions, indicating diminished repair of O4-alkyldT lesions. Together, we identify HMGB1 and HMGB2 as O4-alkyldT recognition proteins, and our work suggests the functions of these proteins in promoting the repair of O4-alkyldT lesions.

title: Cascade-Amplified Microfluidic Detection of Tumor Biomarkers via Metal-DNA Nanospheres Activating CRISPR-Cas12a Assay.
authors: Zhao, Wenjian; Luan, Xiaowei; Long, Wenxiu; Li, Zhi; Dong, Ping; He, Bangshun; Gao, Yanfeng; Liu, Hongmei; Yin, Yi; Song, Yujun
abstract: The development of ultrasensitive protein detection platforms is pivotal for early cancer diagnosis, yet existing methods are often constrained by inefficient "protein-to-signal" conversion and complex instrumentation. While CRISPR-Cas-based biosensors offer higher sensitivity for nucleic acids, their application in protein analysis is fundamentally limited by the low nucleic acid loading capacity and tedious functionalization of traditional inorganic signal carriers such as gold nanoparticles and metal-organic frameworks (MOFs). Herein, we report a highly efficient signal-transduction strategy utilizing Fe-coordinated DNA nanospheres (FDNSs) horizontal line a programmable, metal-nucleic acid assembly horizontal line as a high-capacity DNA reservoir for amplified biomarker sensing. Unlike conventional surface-modified inorganic nanoparticles, the solid-core FDNSs achieve an unprecedented DNA loading density and exhibit specific stimulus-responsive degradation. In this FACC (FDNS-activated CRISPR chip) platform, the recognition of tumor biomarkers triggers the rapid collapse of FDNSs, releasing a massive flux of barcode DNA that subsequently activates the CRISPR-Cas12a system within a microfluidic device. This dual-amplification architecture enables the ultrasensitive quantification of prostate-specific antigen (PSA) and carcinoembryonic antigen (CEA) with detection limits of 0.028 fg/mL and 0.0265 fg/mL, respectively. By replacing complex inorganic carriers with this programmable DNA assembly, our platform simplifies the sensing workflow and significantly enhances sensitivity, providing a robust and portable solution for cancer screening in resource-limited settings.

title: Highly Sensitive Electrochemical Biosensing Strategy Based on Multiple CRISPR/Cas12a Trans-Cleavage Units.
authors: Chai, Hua; Ye, Weifeng; You, Honglan; Yan, Ruhong; Miao, Peng
abstract: This study presents the assembly of multiple CRISPR/Cas12a units by target-induced hybridization chain reaction (HCR), which is capable of highly sensitive electrochemical detection of target miRNA. The confinement effect of the HCR/Cas12a system is demonstrated, which shows significantly improved cleavage compared with the single Cas12a unit. The tetrahedral DNA nanostructure on the surface of the electrode supports the substrate for cleavage, which possesses the merits of excellent reactivity and accessibility. Because of the dual signal amplification, a low limit of detection down to 2.1 aM is achieved. This method also exhibits excellent specificity, storage stability, and accuracy, indicating its value for miRNA sensing in real biological samples and related clinical applications.

title: AI-Guided Engineering of Tunable CcdB Variants for Flexible Selection in Escherichia coli.
authors: Li, Pengpai; Wang, Hongle; Fan, Xiangrui; Zhang, Fa; Lv, Jiugong; Tan, Huiping; Liang, Liya; Liu, Rongming
abstract: The strong cytotoxicity of wild-type CcdB limits its use as a counter-selection marker, as leaky expression can cause unintended cell death. Here, we report the rational engineering of a tunable CcdB variant with minimal basal toxicity while retaining inducible lethality. Using a structure-aware deep learning-guided strategy, we prioritized mutations predicted to alter CcdB-DNA gyrase binding energetics and experimentally identified variants with reduced basal toxicity and retained inducible killing. Targeted validation identified CcdB_L96P, which significantly reduces basal toxicity while preserving effective killing upon induction. This variant exhibits minimal leakage and robust inducible lethality across multiple Escherichia coli strains without requiring specialized hosts. It enables antibiotic-free CRISPR gRNA plasmid construction with high accuracy and efficient enrichment of correctly assembled clones. In a succinic acid-producing chassis, CcdB_L96P imposes no detectable metabolic burden and supports effective removal of residual cells using low concentrations of anhydrotetracycline. Together, this work provides a generalizable protein-level strategy for tuning toxin activity in synthetic biology.

title: Reprogramming Enfumafungin Biosynthesis for High-Titer Production in the Endophytic Fungus Hormonema carpetanum ATCC 74360.
authors: Wo, Jing; Yu, Haipeng; Yang, Yige; Wu, Hongxi; Xiong, Fangjie; Kong, Dekun
abstract: Enfumafungin is the essential precursor for the FDA-approved antifungal agent Ibrexafungerp, yet its production is hindered by low yields, restrictive solid-state fermentation, and the genetic intractability of its producer strain, Hormonema carpetanum ATCC 74360. Here, we developed a CRISPR/Cas9-mediated platform that halved the genetic iteration cycle to less than 15 days. By rewiring the biosynthetic cluster through promoter engineering, we successfully transitioned production to scalable liquid fermentation, achieving an initial 21.6 mg/L. Then, the mevalonate pathway genes (tHMGR, ERG9, and ERG1) were overexpressed, which successfully boosted the titer to 250.1 mg/L. Following medium optimization, the engineered strain HC07 reached a record-breaking 592.4 mg/L in 250 mL shake flasks, the highest yield achieved via metabolic engineering to date. This study provides a robust microbial platform and a streamlined genetic toolbox, paving the way for the sustainable biomanufacturing of next-generation triterpenoid antifungals.

title: A Novel, Simple, and Highly Efficient Dual-sgRNA CRISPR/Cas9-Based Editing System in the Filamentous Fungus Fusarium oxysporum.
authors: Zhu, Wangjie; Liao, Jiaoqun; Liu, Yuanyuan; Zhang, Huawei
abstract: Fusarium oxysporum, as one of the most common filamentous fungi, possesses great biosynthetic potential for natural products. However, the lack of efficient genetic tools has hindered functional genome mining and metabolic engineering in this fungus. In this study, a novel highly efficient CRISPR/Cas9-based dual-sgRNA expression editing system for F. oxysporum was successfully developed through construction of a robust plasmid platform pFRCas9-G418 using incorporation of an endogenous histone H2B nuclear localization signal and a 5S rRNA promoter-driven polycistronic tRNA-sgRNA cassette. This system is suitable not only for single-gene editing but also for large-fragment deletion and multiplex gene editing, although the editing efficiency is somewhat lower. First, this new CRISPR/Cas9 system exhibited a high efficiency of 93.75% +/- 6.25% for deletion of the Fusarium cyclin C1 (fcc1) gene ( approximately 1 kb), which was usually selected as the target gene responsible for yellow pigment accumulation. Then, knockout of the core NRPS gene sanB ( approximately 19 kb) and knock-in of the strong promoter gpdA in the N-methylsansalvamide (SA) biosynthetic gene cluster (BGC) in strain F. oxysporum R1 using this system, respectively, led to no SA yield and an increase of 26.4% SA titer, confirming its capacity for large gene deletion and gene knock-in. Furthermore, one-step dual-gene knockout of hat1 (histone acetyltransferase gene,  approximately 1.5 kb) and pacC (pH-responsive transcription factor,  approximately 2 kb) was first achieved in Fusarium species. This versatile platform provides a powerful tool for editing gene(s) of various sizes in F. oxysporum.

title: Paving the Way for a Minimal CHO ChassisExploring the Upper Limits of Megabase-Scale Deletions through DNA Repair Modulation.
authors: Brauer, Melina; Walker, Emely; Schneider, Stefan; Weiss, Linus; Geiger, Anna; Lindner, Benjamin; Hadicke, Oliver; Schmidt, Moritz; Fischer, Simon; Otte, Kerstin
abstract: Chinese hamster ovary (CHO) cells are the predominant mammalian host for therapeutic protein production, yet their large genome contains substantial non-essential DNA that may impose metabolic burden and contribute to process variability. Here, we establish a CRISPR/Cas9-based strategy for megabase-scale genomic deletions in CHO cells, targeting regions from 3 to over 100 megabases (Mb). Clones carrying deletions of up to 50 Mb were isolated, while a candidate deletion junction spanning 130 Mb was detected in the edited pool, demonstrating the potential for large-scale genome engineering in mammalian cells. Importantly, removal of genomic regions with minimal coding content did not impair growth, viability, or monoclonal antibody productivity. Mechanistic analysis revealed rapid deletion formation and a size-dependent shift in DNA repair pathway usage. Transient inhibition of non-homologous end joining (NHEJ) significantly improved deletion efficiency and clone recovery without compromising cell fitness. These findings establish large-scale genome reduction as a feasible and controllable strategy for rational CHO genome streamlining and the development of next-generation biopharmaceutical cell factories.

title: DeepCRISPR-Typer: Accurate CRISPR-Cas Identification and Subtyping in Metagenomes via Integrated Deep Learning.
authors: Wen, Long; Jing, Minghui; Li, Yanyan; Shang, Xuequn; Liao, Xingyu
abstract: Accurate identification and classification of CRISPR-Cas systems are crucial for understanding microbial immune mechanisms and developing novel genome-editing tools. However, traditional homology-based mining methods face severe computational bottlenecks and assembly fragmentation challenges when processing massive metagenomic data. Here, we present DeepCRISPR-Typer, a comprehensive computational framework integrating a large protein language model (TEMC-Cas), a deep sequence feature extractor (CRISPR-RepTyper), and an adaptive targeted HMM profiling strategy. DeepCRISPR-Typer integrates array and Cas evidence and significantly reduces computational overhead by dynamically invoking subtype-specific HMM subsets. In metagenomic dataset evaluations, DeepCRISPR-Typer achieved a classification accuracy of 94.26% and demonstrated a significant acceleration of approximately 1 orders of magnitude compared to existing mainstream tools. This research provides a robust and scalable engine for metagenome-scale CRISPR system discovery, significantly expanding the mining toolbox for genome engineering applications.

title: Engineering DNA-Targeting CRISPR and CRISPR-Like Effectors: Advances from Rational Design and High-Throughput Screening to AI-Driven Development.
authors: She, Lingwei; Liang, Zeyu; Zou, Qin; Huo, Yi-Xin
abstract: Clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeats (CRISPR) and CRISPR-associated (Cas) proteins constitute adaptive immune systems in prokaryotes and have transformed life sciences, precision medicine, and synthetic biology as programmable genome-editing tools. Despite their broad utility, naturally occurring DNA-targeting Cas effectors remain constrained by several intrinsic limitations, including large protein size that complicates delivery, stringent protospacer adjacent motif (PAM) requirements that restrict targetable genomic space, and mismatch tolerance that can lead to off-target activity and potential genotoxicity. These challenges have made Cas protein engineering and the discovery of novel CRISPR and CRISPR-like systems from metagenomic resources central to the development of next-generation genome-editing platforms. This Review places recent advances within an integrated synthetic biology engineering continuum that links natural effector discovery, structure-guided hypothesis generation, high-throughput functional screening, machine learning-enabled model construction, and iterative redesign. This Review summarizes progress in the screening, optimization, and functional engineering of DNA-targeting CRISPR and CRISPR-like effectors, with emphasis on structure-guided rational design, directed evolution coupled with high-throughput screening, bioinformatics- and evolution-guided mining of novel systems from large-scale sequence databases, and artificial intelligence-assisted development. By integrating these strategies, we highlight how CRISPR effector engineering is moving toward design-build-test-learn (DBTL)-inspired workflows that expand the functional landscape of genome-editing technologies and advance genome editing toward improved efficiency, safety, and programmability.

title: Invasive RNA Programs Optical Switching in DNA Nanoclusters for CRISPR Sensing.
authors: Gold, Reggie; Imtiaz, Yusha; Morya, Vinod; Halvorsen, Ken; Hanson, Emmett; Yigit, Mehmet V
abstract: DNA-templated silver nanoclusters have regained attention due to recent advances in stability and tunable optical properties. Here, we report a highly regulated DNA-templated silver nanocluster (DFN2) that exhibits strong fluorescence at 561 nm and enables reversible, label-free fluorescence switching governed by nucleic acid hybridization. The fluorescence of DFN2 is efficiently quenched with complementary DNA or RNA and fully restored through invading RNA strand mediated displacement, enabling robust and programmable ON-OFF-ON optical control. We integrated this hybridization-responsive platform with CRISPR-Cas12a to construct a target-activated biosensing system. Upon recognition of a conserved genomic fragment from a foodborne pathogen Listeria monocytogenes, the activated Cas12a cleaves a regulator DNA, initiating a cascade of hybridization and strand-displacement reactions that restore nanocluster fluorescence through an invasive RNA. This strategy exhibits high specificity against conserved genomic regions from other foodborne pathogens. These findings establish DFN2 as programmable, enzyme-responsive optical reporters for rapid, sensitive, and modular point-of-care biosensing.

title: Metal-Organic Framework-Assisted CRISPR/Cas12a System for Biosensing: Advances, Challenges, and Perspectives.
authors: Wei, Luyu; Sun, Xueyan; Zhao, Xihong; Wang, Zhilong

title: Cell-Surface-to-Solution Signal Transduction via a CRISPR/Cas12a-Based Dual-Target Aptamer Sensor for Detecting Urothelial Carcinoma Cells in Urine.
authors: Wu, Shun-Li; Shi, Jia-Yi; Tan, Yan; Jiang, Hong-Xin; Hou, Xiao-Yun; Liu, Shuang-Qing; Li, Kai-Di; Sun, Wen-Bo; Li, Man-Ying; Zhu, Li Na; Cai, Qi-Liang; Kong, De-Ming
abstract: Urothelial carcinoma (UC) is a common malignancy of the genitourinary system with high recurrence rates, requiring non-invasive postoperative monitoring. Direct detection of exfoliated UC cells in urine can provide tumor-origin evidence but remains challenging because of low target-cell abundance, complex urine interference, and subjective cytological interpretation. Herein, we developed a CRISPR/Cas12a-based dual-target aptamer sensor for sensitive and specific detection of exfoliated UC cells in urine. The sensing system spatially couples CKAP4-mediated magnetic capture with PD-L1-dependent retention of a Cas12a activator on the same captured cell. Magnetic washing removes unbound activator probes, whereas the cell-retained activator subsequently initiates Cas12a trans-cleavage in the solution-phase reaction. This capture-retain-activate architecture provides an AND-gate-like route for converting spatially coupled cell-surface recognition events into an amplified fluorescence output. The sensor achieved a detection limit of 12 cells per assay and showed good selectivity against interfering cells. A pilot clinical evaluation using 32 urine samples distinguished UC patients from non-UC individuals with an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.996. This work provides a capture-retain-activate strategy for the non-invasive analysis of intact exfoliated UC cells and illustrates a potential design route for coupling cell-surface recognition with solution-phase CRISPR/Cas12a signal amplification.

title: RNase H-Assisted, Split-crRNA-Based CRISPR/Cas12a Lateral Flow Assay for Amplification-Free, Multi-Site Detection of Bacterial 16S rRNA.
authors: Min, Yoo-Hong; Lee, Deok-Gyu; Yoo, Jin-Hee; Shin, Yong-Beom; Byun, Ju-Young
abstract: With the growing demand for on-site testing of foodborne pathogens, rapid and sensitive detection methods are urgently needed. Here, we developed a split-crRNA-based CRISPR/Cas12a assay integrated with a lateral flow assay (sCR-LFA) for rapid, sensitive detection of bacterial 16S rRNA within 1 h, without pre-amplification. To detect highly structured 16S rRNA, we used RNA fragmentation via DNA-helper-mediated RNase H pretreatment. When short RNA targets interact with corresponding RNA blockers, unblocked RNA spacers hybridize with a DNA activator to form spacer/activator duplexes, which activate split-crRNA/Cas12a complexes. The sCR-LFA achieved a detection limit of 104 CFU/mL for single-site targeting. Using an enhanced sCR-LFA that integrates a multi-site targeting strategy, we achieved a lower detection limit of 102 CFU/mL. Furthermore, the enhanced sCR-LFA was successfully validated in simulated milk and mushroom samples spiked with bacteria. Collectively, this work presents a promising approach for effective food safety monitoring and prevention of infectious diseases.

title: CHAI-sEV: A Programmable Hairpin-Driven Cas9 Platform with AI Integration for Dual-Protein Profiling and Intelligent Classification of Tumor-Derived Small Extracellular Vesicles.
authors: Shen, Haoyu; Pan, Xinyu; Wu, Yan; Chen, Bing; Zhou, Xiaolei; Qiao, Linbo; Effah, Clement Yaw; Zhou, Jing; Yu, Junying; Zhang, Zhenzhong; Yang, Xiaonan; Wu, Yongjun; Ding, Lihua
abstract: Multiplexed protein profiling of tumor-derived small extracellular vesicles (TsEVs) requires signal-conversion strategies that are sensitive, low-background, and orthogonal. Collateral-cleavage CRISPR assays based on Cas12a or Cas13a provide efficient amplification but can compromise single-pot multitarget detection, whereas the sequence-specific cleavage of Cas9 remains underexplored for converting vesicle-surface protein recognition into orthogonal amplified outputs. Here, we report CHAI-sEV, a programmable Cas9-mediated trigger-release strategy based on PAM-bearing hairpin-locking probes (PHLPs) for dual-protein profiling of TsEVs. Each PHLP integrates Cas9 recognition and signal conversion into a single molecular substrate, in which sgRNA-guided Cas9 cleavage unlocks a sequestered CHA activator to initiate orthogonal signal amplification. After EGFR- or PD-L1-binding aptamers label TsEVs, engineered aptamer tails recruit specific Cas9-sgRNA complexes to the vesicle surface, enabling protein-specific PHLP activation and amplified fluorescence readout. This Cas9-programmed trigger-release mechanism enables dual-channel TsEV protein detection without relying on nonspecific collateral cleavage. Under optimized conditions, CHAI-sEV achieved detection limits of 162 and 328 particles/muL for EGFR and PD-L1. In plasma samples, CHAI-sEV differentiated lung cancer patients from benign-lung-disease patients and healthy controls and showed decreased EGFR and PD-L1 signals in post-treatment samples. As proof-of-concept extensions, the CHAI-sEV was further coupled to an IGZO-FET electrical readout and an exploratory machine-learning analysis combining dual-protein signals with clinical features. Overall, PHLPs provide a substrate-design principle that converts Cas9 cleavage into amplification-compatible and orthogonally multiplexable biosensing outputs, enabling sensitive and multiplexed protein profiling of TsEVs and offering potential for extension to diverse molecular targets.

title: Engineering a Transcription Activation Toolkit by Rewiring Prokaryotic Transcription Factors and Synthetic Yeast Promoters in Yarrowia lipolytica.
authors: Li, Yunhe; Wei, Wenping; Zhang, Ping; Huang, Ting; Shang, Yanzhe; Zhou, Ying; Ye, Bang-Ce
journal: Journal of agricultural and food chemistry
abstract: Yarrowia lipolytica is a promising industrial host, yet its metabolic engineering potential remains limited by insufficient genetic tools. Here, we engineered a synthetic Transcription Activation Toolkit (TAT) based on LacI-VPRH, a chimeric protein fusing the prokaryotic DNA-binding domain LacI with the eukaryotic activation domain VPRH. Systematic optimization of LacO copy numbers and core promoter composition achieved up to 205-fold gene activation. The TAT platform was further expanded to construct bidirectional expression systems and enable multiplexed gene control. Applied to resveratrol biosynthesis via a "push-pull" strategy, CRISPR/Cas9-mediated integration of TAT-controlled synthetic promoters upregulated the shikimate pathway genes aroM10 and aroC alongside the rate-limiting enzyme ST1, achieving a shake-flask titer of 2.715 g/L horizontal line the highest reported to date. Additionally, an IPTG-inducible "turn-on" system (TAT-2.0) incorporating the antiLacI9 mutant was developed for small-molecule-responsive transcriptional control. Collectively, the modular TAT system provides a versatile strategy for precise metabolic pathway optimization in Y. lipolytica.

title: Rational Design of Modular Elastin-like Polypeptide Nanoparticles for Nonviral Gene Delivery.
authors: Qu, Feng; Thompson, David H
abstract: Gene therapy has evolved into a cornerstone modality in modern medicine, with applications spanning antisense oligonucleotide treatments, RNA interference therapies, mRNA vaccines, in vivo CAR-T cell therapies, and CRISPR-mediated in vivo gene editing. The demands of this proliferating therapeutic approach compel the development of delivery systems that excel in achieving target specificity, repeat dosing compatibility, storage stability, and scalable manufacturability. Although viral vectors and lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) have achieved clinical success, they face inherent challenges in fully meeting these evolving requirements, highlighting the need for alternatives. Nonviral gene delivery is a highly complex process that requires the delivery system to strike the proper balance between plasma and shelf stability, appropriate kinetic response for cargo release in the target biological milieu, and capacity for resorption or clearance from the body to minimize acute and/or long-term toxicity. Elastin-like polypeptides (ELPs), derived from human tropoelastin motifs, have emerged as promising scaffolds due to their tunable properties, low immunogenicity, and biodegradable nature. A growing number of laboratories are embracing the potential of ELPs to advance novel gene delivery systems toward these goals. This Account describes our laboratory's sustained contributions in the ELP field over the past decade, culminating in the layer-by-layer elastin-like polypeptide nucleic acid nanoparticle (LENN) platform, which is a modular and biomanufacturable nonviral gene delivery system. We pioneered a fast organic solvent extraction-precipitation purification for ELPs that is sequence independent, yields material with low endotoxin levels, and preserves the functionality of fusion domains. LENN assembly is achieved by the electrostatic condensation of nucleic acids using cyclodextrin-polyarginine conjugates to form the core, followed by coating with ELP shells through reversible host-guest interactions, producing nanoparticles capable of high RNA encapsulation. This Account presents a head-to-head design comparison of LENN versus LNPs, representative peptide-based vectors, and polymeric nonviral systems, illustrating the modularity of LENN that allows for independent optimization of key functional elements. Targeted LENN undergoes rapid internalization and endosomal escape in EGFR+ bladder cancer cells, enabling efficient mRNA expression and siRNA knockdown. Mechanistic studies confirm cellular entry via the clathrin-mediated uptake pathway and activation of lipid remodeling processes that facilitate cargo release. In an initial proof-of-concept study, EGF-modified LENN exhibited tumor association following intravesical administration in orthotopic bladder cancer models. These studies illustrate the modularity of the LENN design and its potential as a tunable, biocompatible platform for nucleic acid therapeutics.

title: CRISPR/Cas12a-powered self-sustaining catalytic nucleic acid circuit for highly sensitive detection of aflatoxin B1.
authors: Wu, Zhihui; Ma, Yucong; Li, Xiangzhi; Yan, Zhengyu; Huang, Yu; Wang, Kaiqiang; Quan, Wei; Mo, Lan; Liu, Shi Gang
abstract: Aflatoxin B1 (AFB1) is a highly toxic mycotoxin and strongly carcinogenic and teratogenic to humans. Achieving CRISPR-based sensing system for highly sensitive detection of AFB1 remains a significant challenge. A CRISPR/Cas12a-powered self-sustaining catalytic nucleic acid circuit (CPSCN) is proposed for the sensitive and accurate detection of aflatoxin B1 (AFB1). In the CPSCN sensing system, CRISPR/Cas12a/gRNA1 indirectly recognizes AFB1 by aptamer and effectively triggers trans-cleavage of a pair of self-reporting single-stranded DNA-locked RNA2 fluorescence probes (named as dual-winged fluorescence probe). The released RNA2 then initiates an autocatalytic positive feedback loop, resulting in continuous probe cleavage. The CPSCN system achieves highly sensitive detection in a single-enzyme one-step process. The method exhibits excellent quantitative capability for AFB1 detection with a detection limit of 7.5 pg/mL. In real samples, the detection results of the proposed biosensor show high consistency with those obtained by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA). This work not only provides a novel strategy for AFB1 detection with high sensitivity, robustness, and operational simplicity, but also offers a new insight for designing signal amplification strategies of CRISPR-based biosensors.

title: PHLDA3 deficiency attenuates neonatal sepsis-associated acute lung injury and is associated with reduced endoplasmic reticulum stress and NF-kappaB activation.
authors: Liu, Jue; Zhang, Zubin; Lu, Liang Hua; Feng, Chenxi; Kong, Yu; Tu, Daman; Xu, Li-Xiao; Qin, Zheng-Hong; Sun, Bin; Feng, Xing; Li, Mei
abstract: Neonatal sepsis often causes acute lung injury (ALI), but the underlying molecular mechanisms of ALI have not been elucidated. Pleckstrin homology-like domain family A member 3 (PHLDA3) is a stress-responsive protein involved in inflammatory signaling, yet its role in neonatal sepsis-associated ALI has not been explored. Here, we established a neonatal polymicrobial sepsis model via intraperitoneal injection of cecal slurry (CS) and investigated the role of PHLDA3 in ALI using CRISPR/Cas9-generated constitutive PHLDA3 knockout (PHLDA3 KO) mice. CS induced time-dependent upregulation of PHLDA3 in neonatal lung tissues. CS triggered significant increases in the levels of IL-1beta, IL-6, and TNF-alpha in lung tissues, impairing vascular integrity and causing severe alveolar damage. These harmful effects were alleviated by PHLDA3 KO. Transcriptomic analysis revealed enrichment of endoplasmic reticulum (ER) protein processing pathways. CS activated ER stress and unfolded protein response via PERK/eIF2alpha/ATF4 and ATF6 axes, which were attenuated by PHLDA3 deletion. Pharmacological induction of ER stress by thapsigargin (TG) reversed the protective effects of PHLDA3 KO, whereas ER stress inhibitor 4-phenylbutyric acid (4-PBA) mitigated inflammation and lung injury. In macrophage models, PHLDA3 knockdown was associated with reduced LPS-induced ER-stress-related signaling, NF-kappaB activation, and inflammatory responses, whereas TG attenuated these effects. Collectively, these findings indicate that constitutive PHLDA3 deficiency is associated with attenuated neonatal sepsis-associated lung injury, reduced ER-stress-related signaling, and decreased NF-kappaB activation, and support further investigation of PHLDA3 in neonatal sepsis-associated ALI.

title: Leveraging high temperature for enhanced and faster detection of SARS-CoV-2 and its Omicron variant with CRISPR-AsCas12a.
authors: Moreno, Melissa Morales; Zacarias, Jessica; Garcia, Idalia; Garcia, Mario Alanis; Valdes, Erick Gustavo; Hernandez-Garcia, Armando
journal: Journal of pharmaceutical and biomedical analysis
abstract: CRISPR-based methods are effective for detecting SARS-CoV-2, with performance comparable to gold-standard PCR. Developing simpler, faster, and more sensitive CRISPR-based diagnostics will accelerate their adoption in field. Adjusting the temperature at which Cas proteins operate is crucial for enhancing DNA recognition kinetics, thereby improving specificity, sensitivity, and practicality. However, optimization is challenging due to the narrow temperature range for activity of wild-type Cas orthologs. Here, we show that heating the wild-type AsCas12a protein above its optimal temperature, up to 65 masculineC, accelerates nucleic acid detection, reducing the limit of detection (LoD) by 33-fold without causing false positives. This effect was further enhanced by buffer optimization. We applied these conditions to develop a two-step fluorescence- and lateral flow strip-based method for detecting SARS-CoV-2 in as little as 5 min from LAMP amplicons, and demonstrated its applicability for discriminating the Omicron variant from the wild-type strain using plasmid DNA. Overall, these findings demonstrate that increasing reaction temperature is a simple, effective strategy to enhance CRISPR-Cas12a diagnostics for pathogens, without the need for protein engineering or thermophilic Cas12a orthologs.

title: Lysine analogue-driven adaptive evolution produces lysine-overproducing wine yeast strains.
authors: Muniz-Calvo, Sara; Valera-Garcia, Elena; Pardo, Judit; Vazquez, Maria; Planells-Carcel, Andres; Alonso-Del-Real, Javier; Su, Ying; Heras, Jose Maria; Ortiz-Julien, Anne; Garcia-Rios, Estefani; Guillamon, Jose M
abstract: Lysine, though a poor nitrogen source for Saccharomyces cerevisiae, is rapidly consumed during wine fermentation and has been linked to enhanced oxidative and sulfur dioxide resistance. To investigate and harness this phenotype, the industrial wine strain P14 was subjected to adaptive laboratory evolution under increasing concentrations of the toxic lysine analogue S-aminoethyl cysteine (AEC). The resulting evolved isolates accumulated up to tenfold more intracellular lysine, displayed elevated reduced glutathione, and exhibited substantially decreased ROS levels while maintaining robust fermentation performance. Whole-genome sequencing revealed extensive genomic rearrangements and recurrent mutations associated with lysine biosynthesis. Among these, the LYS21(V127F) mutation emerged as the major driver of lysine overproduction and AEC resistance. CRISPR/Cas9 reconstruction of this allele in multiple wine yeasts confirmed its causal role and conferred a competitive advantage during fermentation. These findings demonstrate the effectiveness of AEC-driven evolution for generating lysine-overproducing wine yeasts and highlight LYS21 feedback-resistance as a key metabolic innovation.

title: Lactic acid bacteria bacteriocins: From antimicrobial mechanisms to next-generation applications in the food industry.
authors: Liu, Zhineng; Yin, Yankun; Liu, Yuxin; Kang, Xihui; Yin, Jie; Han, Li; Lan, Cong
abstract: Lactic acid bacteria (LAB) bacteriocins are ribosomally synthesized antimicrobial peptides attracting significant attention as natural alternatives to conventional antibiotics and food preservatives. This review offers a systematic overview of LAB bacteriocin classification and mechanisms of action, highlighting shifts driven by advancements in genomics, synthetic biology, and computational design. Traditional applications in dairy, meat, and beverage products are examined alongside emerging concepts like smart delivery systems and multifunctional formulations. Despite demonstrated efficacy, widespread commercialization of LAB bacteriocins faces challenges such as low production yields, high purification costs, limited antimicrobial spectra, and instability within complex food matrices. Recent advances in genome mining tools, like antiSMASH, have expedited the discovery of novel bacteriocin gene clusters, while CRISPR-based technologies facilitate the metabolic engineering of high-yield producer strains. Computational approaches, including machine learning for activity prediction and generative artificial intelligence (AI) for de novo peptide design, offer unprecedented opportunities to create variants with tailored properties. Integration with stimuli-responsive materials, such as peptide-based hydrogels, promises precise spatial and temporal control of antimicrobial activity in food systems. By outlining a comprehensive development pathway from discovery through to production, design, and application, this review aims to guide the evolution of LAB bacteriocins from promising natural products to versatile, next-generation food preservation tools and beyond.

title: Microfluidic platforms for food analysis: Materials, fabrication, analytical strategies, matrix handling, and translation.
authors: Lu, Guantong; Li, Xiang
abstract: BACKGROUND: Food analysis requires assessment of quality, authenticity, and safety in heterogeneous matrices. Microfluidic platforms can reduce sample and reagent consumption and integrate analytical operations, but chip-level performance does not necessarily translate into representative, reproducible, or field-compatible testing. SCOPE AND APPROACH: This review critically assesses whether reported analytical gains remain meaningful across food-sample-to-result workflows. It connects materials and fabrication with recognition, readout, matrix handling, and testing decisions and compares reported fabrication and analytical metrics. Evidence from naturally contaminated, artificially inoculated or spiked, and pre-purified samples is distinguished. Advances in clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeats (CRISPR), magnetofluidics, and artificial intelligence (AI) are assessed by their gains and remaining limitations. KEY FINDINGS AND CONCLUSIONS: Reported detection limits and assay times often cover only on-chip stages, while sampling, matrix preparation, and reader requirements remain external or excluded. Spiked or purified inputs provide less direct evidence than naturally contaminated foods. Sensitivity, multiplexing, and automation gains may increase calibration, instrumentation, and manufacturing burdens. Poly(dimethylsiloxane) (PDMS) with soft lithography favors prototyping, printed paper supports low-cost screening, and injection-molded thermoplastics support high-volume production of reproducible closed cartridges. CRISPR, magnetofluidics, and AI have expanded sequence specificity, workflow automation, and data interpretation, respectively, but do not remove preparation and validation constraints. The transition from heterogeneous food lots to microliter volumes is a central bottleneck linked to pretreatment, manufacture, and validation. A food-specific strengths, weaknesses, opportunities, and threats (SWOT) analysis supports staged priorities in representative sampling and matrix-compatible pretreatment, enclosed multiparameter automation and cost-controlled manufacture, and reference-method comparison and interlaboratory validation.

title: Umami-active components in edible Fungi: Distribution, structure-function relationships, molecular mechanisms, computational insights and industrial applications.
authors: Khengle, Samruddhi; Kalam, Tejas; Mondal, Imdadul Hoque; Sherin, Zincia; Bashir, Omar; Pawase, Prashant Anil; Kapila, Akshit
abstract: Edible mushrooms are a biodiverse yet underutilized source of umami compounds providing clean-label alternatives to synthetic flavourings such as monosodium glutamate (MSG). The characteristic savory taste arises from interactions among free amino acids (glutamate, aspartate), 5'-ribonucleotides (5'-GMP, 5'-IMP), organic acids (succinic, citric), polyols (trehalose, mannitol), and bioactive peptides, whose accumulation is influenced by genetic composition, growth substrate, developmental stage, and postharvest management. This review systematically examines the distribution of umami compounds in Pleurotus spp., Lentinula edodes, Hypsizygus marmoreus, and other species, with emphasis on umami peptides, their structure-function relationships, and taste perception mediated by T1R1/T1R3, mGluR1/mGluR4, and CaSR receptors. In addition, it critically assesses industrial applications and advanced computational approaches including iUmami-SCM, UMPred-FRL, Umami-MRNN, Umami-BERT, molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations for high-throughput discovery of umami peptides. Enzymatic hydrolysis coupled with ultrafiltration enriches low-molecular-weight (<3 kDa) umami peptides while reducing associated bitterness. Equivalent Umami Concentration (EUC) reflects an 8-10-fold synergistic enhancement between amino acids and nucleotides, where the synergistic constant represents the strength of their non-additive umami interaction. While fungal peptides are highly valued for their unique sensory contributions, their significance extends beyond taste as they also exert multifunctional bioactivities including ACE inhibition (IC(5)(0): 9-150 muM), antioxidant activity (DPPH and ABTS assays), and endothelial protection. Challenges include genetic engineering strategies for umami enhancement, salt-umami interactions, and analytical standards. Emerging industrial applications, including CRISPR/Cas9-based metabolic engineering and agro-waste upcycling, position edible fungi as promising platforms for clean-label flavor systems, sodium reduction, and circular food economies.

title: Challenges in Gene-Directed Therapies for Rare Neurodevelopmental Disorders Using HNRNPU as an Exemplar.
authors: Aiyedun, Daniel; Rogers, Susan F; Taha, Doaa M; Balasubramanian, Meena
abstract: Next-generation sequencing has radically transformed the diagnostic capability of rare neurodevelopmental disorders (RNDDs), yet translating these molecular insights into viable therapeutics remains a hurdle. While gene-directed modalities, specifically viral-mediated supplementation, antisense oligonucleotides (ASOs), and CRISPR-based activation or precision editing, offer a means to rescue loss-of-function phenotypes, successful clinical implementation requires moving past the reductive framework of merely increasing the expression of the target gene towards approaches that account for spatial, developmental, and therapeutic windows. This review uses HNRNPU-related rare neurodevelopmental disorder (HNRNPU-RNDD), a condition marked with global developmental delay and refractory epilepsy, as an exemplar to discuss these translational hurdles. We discuss the homeostatic boundaries of this scaffold attachment factor, where unregulated overexpression risks localised cytotoxicity, and altered chromatin dynamics compromise editing safety. Furthermore, we assess how cell-type sensitivity and narrow developmental windows may dictate clinical efficacy. By using HNRNPU-RNDD to critically analyse the challenges of using each therapeutic platform, we hope to inform the creation of gene-directed therapies that aim to treat disorders resulting from structural pleiotropic dosage-sensitive proteins.

title: Overcoming the cutaneous barrier: Topical delivery platforms for targeted gene-based therapeutics in psoriasis.
authors: Lin, Zih-Chan; Lin, Cheng-Yu; Chung, Yu-Kuo; Alalaiwe, Ahmed; Fang, Jia-You
journal: Journal of controlled release : official journal of the Controlled Release Society
abstract: Psoriasis is a chronic immune-mediated skin disorder characterized by persistent inflammation, epidermal hyperproliferation, and complex interactions among immune cells, keratinocytes, cytokines, and genetic factors. Although conventional topical agents, systemic small molecules, and biologics have improved disease management, their clinical utility is often limited by insufficient efficacy, adverse effects, treatment resistance, and poor patient adherence. Recent advances in molecular biology have identified numerous pathogenic genes, signaling pathways, and regulatory RNAs involved in psoriasis, providing opportunities for the development of gene-based therapeutics, including antisense oligonucleotides, plasmid DNAs, small interfering RNAs, messenger RNAs, microRNAs, aptamers, and CRISPR/Cas9 systems. These therapeutics enable precise modulation of disease-associated targets at the genomic and transcriptional levels, offering advantages over conventional pharmacological approaches. However, their topical administration is hindered by the formidable cutaneous barrier, limited skin penetration, poor cellular uptake, and susceptibility to enzymatic degradation. This review summarizes the cellular, molecular, and genetic mechanisms underlying psoriasis pathogenesis and discusses the therapeutic potential of diverse gene-based approaches. Particular emphasis is placed on topical delivery platforms designed to overcome cutaneous barriers, including permeation enhancers, nanocarrier-based systems, and physical enhancement technologies. Recent advances in the integration of these delivery strategies with gene therapeutics for targeted psoriasis treatment are highlighted. Finally, current challenges related to delivery efficiency, long-term safety, manufacturing scalability, and regulatory approval are discussed, together with future perspectives for the clinical translation of topical gene-based therapeutics toward precision psoriasis management.

title: One-pot dual RPA-CRISPR/Cas12a lateral flow biosensor for rapid detection of carbapenemase-producing Klebsiella pneumoniae.
authors: Jin, Ming; Sun, Jing; He, Dan; Shi, Weifeng; Jiang, Jingting; Zhou, Wei; Wu, Zhiyun
abstract: Carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae (CRKP) poses a major public health threat due to high mortality and limited therapeutic options. Rapid and accurate detection of both species identity and resistance determinants is critical for clinical management. Here, we developed a dual-target recombinase polymerase amplification-CRISPR/Cas12a multiplex lateral flow assay (DRC-MLFA) for simultaneous detection of K. pneumoniae and blaKPC in a single reaction. This platform introduces a functionally differentiated dual-channel detection strategy, in which the K. pneumoniae signal is generated directly via RPA-lateral flow readout, while blaKPC detection is achieved through an additional CRISPR/Cas12a-mediated verification step. To enable one-pot integration, suboptimal protospacer adjacent motif (PAM) sequences were employed to delay Cas12a activation, thereby coordinating amplification and CRISPR detection within a single reaction system. Under optimized conditions, the assay achieved dual-target detection within 50 min at 37  degrees C, with a limit of detection of 10(1) CFU/muL and high specificity against non-target pathogens. Validation with 30 clinical samples showed strong concordance with quantitative PCR. This portable and low-cost biosensor provides a practical solution for point-of-care detection of CRKP and establishes a framework for integrating hierarchical specificity control into multiplex CRISPR diagnostics.

title: Genetic dissection of rapid proteolysis identifies TXNDC15 as a key factor of ERAD and lipid homeostasis.
authors: Liu, Yuyang; Yaochai, Michelle Yinfei; Liu, Shanshan; Alwaseem, Hanan; Birsoy, Kivanc
abstract: Biological systems face a constantly changing environment and must swiftly respond to stimuli; yet how cells sense and adapt to environmental and physiological cues is incompletely understood. Short-lived proteins can be rapidly induced upon perturbation, enabling swift activation of adaptive cellular responses. Here, leveraging genome-wide data on protein-transcript correlation, we systematically searched for rapid proteolysis substrates whose abundance reflects the activity of the underlying proteolytic machinery. Focusing on the candidate substrate ABHD2, we performed CRISPR-based genetic screens to dissect its degradation. These screens identified TXNDC15 as an essential factor in MARCHF6-mediated ER-associated protein degradation (ERAD). Mechanistically, TXNDC15 supports substrate exit and degradation from the ER via a catalysis-independent mechanism. Loss of TXNDC15 remodels the ER proteome and lipid homeostasis. Together, our work defines a missing component of ERAD and provides a generalizable strategy to decode post-translational regulatory circuits.

title: Probing the Conformational Dynamics of VeCas9 Using High-Resolution Single-Molecule Junctions.
authors: Zhong, Shichao; Li, Baitao; Ji, Zeyang; Zhang, Jingqi; Zhao, Lihua; Yang, Zhiheng; Wang, Dan; He, Suhang; Guo, Xuefeng
journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
abstract: Gene editing enables precise genetic modifications, revolutionizing disease treatment, crop improvement, and biotechnological innovation. VeCas9, a recently identified CRISPR endonuclease from the Veillonella genus, exhibits a broader protospacer adjacent motif recognition range in comparison with the widely used SpCas9 nuclease. However, its working mechanism and potential applications in gene editing still need to be fully characterized. In this work, by integrating VeCas9 into a graphene-molecule-graphene single-molecule junction platform, we carried out label-free, in situ mechanistic studies of VeCas9 function at the single-molecule level with high temporal resolution. Using this setup, we monitored the dynamic interactions between VeCas9, single-guide RNA, and double-stranded DNA in real time, in both stable and transient binding modes. Through temperature-dependent measurements, we determined the kinetic parameters of key steps in the interaction process. Moreover, a series of double-stranded DNA substrates was employed to examine how various sequence mismatches affect the VeCas9 activity, revealing that its sensitivity depends on the position of the mismatch. More importantly, we directly observed VeCas9-mediated R-loop formation and quantified the time scale of single-base expansion events. These single-molecule observations provide mechanistic insights into the Cas9 function and demonstrate the strong potential of high temporal-resolution single-molecule techniques for studying dynamic biological processes.

title: MITE insertions generate enhancers for iron transporter CwIRT1 activation in citrus.
authors: Zhou, Xingxing; Liu, Shengjun; Fan, Zhengyan; Peng, Jiaxuan; Liu, Chunyi; Wu, Yifang; Xu, Qiang; Xiao, Shunyuan; Pan, Zhiyong
abstract: Iron (Fe) deficiency constrains citrus productivity in alkaline soils. Although the high-affinity Fe transporter IRT1 is essential for Fe acquisition, its transcriptional regulation in citrus remains unclear. Here, we reveal that differential tolerance to Fe deficiency between Fe-sensitive Poncirus trifoliata (P. trifoliata) and Fe-tolerant Citrus wilsonii Tanaka (C. wilsonii) is linked to rapid induction of CwIRT1. We further identify two unique miniature inverted-repeat transposable elements (MITE1 and MITE2) in the promoter region of CwIRT1, which act as Fe-deficiency-responsive enhancers. These two MITEs respectively generate binding sites for the transcription factors CwERF12 and CwARF12, both of which are upregulated under low-Fe conditions. CRISPR/Cas9-mediated dual knockout of CwERF12 and CwARF12, but not single mutations, suppresses CwIRT1 expression and reduces root Fe uptake. We propose that MITEs carrying TF-binding motifs can serve as enhancers recruiting stress-responsive transcription factors to activate CwIRT1, highlighting transposable element-mediated cis-regulatory as a driver of nutrient stress adaptation in perennial crops.

title: From detection to prediction: AI-integrated molecular and biosensing approaches for psychrotrophic and thermophilic spoilage bacteria in dairy systems.
authors: Shamlan, Arzaq; Khan, Mati Ullah; Farid, Anum; Huo, Shengnan; Liu, Hong; Chen, Zhiwei
abstract: Psychrotrophic Gram-negative bacteria and thermophilic or thermoduric spore-forming bacteria are major causes of quality deterioration and shelf-life loss in milk and dairy products. Their impact is mediated primarily by heat-stable peptidases and lipases, heat-resistant spores and biofilms that persist in processing environments; with the notable exception of toxigenic members of the Bacillus cereus group, most of these organisms are spoilage rather than safety hazards. Culture-based methods remain the reference standard but are slow and provide single time-point information. This review critically evaluates molecular and sensing methods, including quantitative and digital PCR, isothermal amplification, CRISPR-Cas assays, biosensors, viability assays, spectroscopy and (meta)omics, with explicit attention to whether performance has been demonstrated in naturally contaminated dairy matrices rather than in buffer or spiked samples, and examines how their outputs could inform predictive microbiology and machine learning. A classification framework based on growth-temperature range, heat resistance, sporulation and dairy relevance is provided, and each detection-to-prediction pathway is graded as demonstrated in dairy, partly demonstrated or proposed. Validated dairy applications currently exist mainly for individual detection assays and for mechanistic or stochastic shelf-life models driven by culture-derived data; prospective, validated workflows in which molecular or biosensor outputs are used as model inputs to forecast spoilage have not yet been reported. Because heat-stable enzymes can spoil ultra-high-temperature products after the producing cells have been inactivated, viable counts alone are insufficient predictors of such defects. Key barriers include matrix effects, small and imbalanced datasets, domain shift, limited external validation and poorly defined intended use. Detection-to-prediction integration should therefore be regarded as an emerging research direction rather than an established industrial capability.

title: Generation of Spinocerebellar Ataxia 27B iPSC Lines and Isogenic Controls.
authors: Chng, Veronica Siew Leng; Davies, Kayli C; Vlahos, Katerina; Howden, Sara E; Bozaoglu, Kiymet; Thompson, Genevieve C; Read, Justin L; Delatycki, Martin; Lockhart, Paul J
abstract: Spinocerebellar Ataxia 27B (SCA27B) is a late-onset neurodegenerative disorder caused by a heterozygous pathogenic GAA*TTC repeat expansion in intron 1 of FGF14. Despite being a common genetic cause of adult-onset cerebellar ataxia, the underlying molecular mechanisms remain unclear. Here, we performed simultaneous reprogramming and CRISPR-Cas9 genome editing to generate four induced pluripotent stem cell (iPSC) lines and their respective isogenic gene-corrected controls. All lines exhibited normal karyotypes, pluripotency, and trilineage differentiation capacity. These paired iPSC lines provide a valuable platform for investigating the pathomechanism(s) of SCA27B and can be used for screening of potential therapeutic treatments.

title: Target-triggered exponential amplification-enhanced CRISPR/Cas12a system with a fluorescence-quenching lateral flow assay for ultrasensitive detection of Salmonella typhimurium.
authors: Xiong, Yuanqian; Li, Li; Huang, Jun; Shen, Xuan-Ang; Sun, Jiayi; Guo, Yuqian; Liu, Daofeng; Ma, Tongtong; Huang, Xiaolin; Xiong, Yonghua
abstract: The use of the CRISPR/Cas12a system combined with lateral flow assays shows significant promise for point-of-care testing in resource-limited regions. However, the use of isothermal amplification technologies to preenrich target DNA fragments inherently increases the risk of aerosol contamination during strip testing. Here, we introduce a target-triggered exponential amplification-enhanced CRISPR/Cas12a system combined with a fluorescence-quenching lateral flow assay (TEA-FQLFA) for ultrasensitive detection of Salmonella typhimurium. The TEA system converts a single Cas12a recognition event into sequential dual Cas12a activation, initiating a cleavage cascade amplification that achieves a 10(6)-fold signal enhancement without the need for a target DNA preamplification operation. Moreover, hyperbranched gold-coated polymer microspheres (HGPMs), characterized by ultrahigh extinction coefficients and a broad absorption band in the 300-800 nm range, are utilized as fluorescence quenching reporters of the FQLFA for simultaneous colorimetric visualization and fluorescence-based quantitative detection of target DNA concentration. By leveraging the synergistic integration of TEA-mediated signal amplification and HGPM-enabled optical signal enhancement, the TEA-FQLFA system achieves attomolar-level detection of target DNA (0.081 aM) and enables sensitive detection of Salmonella typhimurium in complex food matrices, with detection limits of 7.95 CFU/mL in colorimetric mode and 6.94 CFU/mL in fluorescence mode. In summary, this work establishes a versatile platform that integrates cascade signal amplification with dual-mode lateral-flow for ultrasensitive food safety detection.

title: Fiber-2 induces autolysosome dysfunction and impairs autophagic flux to promote FAdV-4 replication.
authors: Sun, Qinqin; Zhang, Lianshun; Liu, Yutong; Chen, Junze; Zheng, Siting; Liu, Lijin; Xie, Honglin; Fu, Qiang
abstract: Fowl adenovirus serotype 4 (FAdV-4) causes hepatitis-hydropericardium syndrome in poultry, yet viral subversion of host autophagy remains unclear. Here, we investigated the role of the viral structural protein Fiber-2 in modulating the host autophagy-lysosome pathway. Transcriptomic profiling of LMH cells expressing Fiber-2 revealed coordinated upregulation of autophagy-related genes, validated by quantitative PCR. Functional assays demonstrated that Fiber-2 expression leads to autophagosome accumulation and impaired autophagic flux, as shown by LC3-II/p62 analysis, tandem fluorescent LC3 reporter imaging, Bafilomycin A1 treatment, and transmission electron microscopy. Fiber-2 predominantly localizes to late endosomes and lysosomes, and GFP-Galectin-3 reporter assays indicate that it disrupts lysosomal membrane integrity rather than blocking autophagosome-lysosome fusion. Co-immunoprecipitation (Co-IP) and enrichment analyses identified BECN1, a key autophagy regulator, as a Fiber-2-interacting protein, and associated host proteins were enriched in autophagy-related pathways. Finally, CRISPR/Cas9-mediated deletion of Fiber-2 significantly reduced FAdV-4 replication at later stages of infection, consistent with a proviral role for Fiber-2. These findings indicate that Fiber-2 disrupts autophagic flux by inducing lysosomal dysfunction and membrane damage, thereby promoting FAdV-4 replication and uncovering a previously unrecognized mechanism of viral subversion of host degradative pathways.

title: Triphenyl phosphate promotes PXR-associated, MEN1-dependent exposure-conditioned enzalutamide tolerance in prostate cancer.
authors: Wu, Wenbo; Niu, Zhuohan; Gao, Feng; Wang, Kunpeng; Wang, Hui; Zong, Dayuan; Lu, Zhongwen; Xue, Peng
abstract: Androgen receptor pathway inhibitors (ARPIs) prolong survival in prostate cancer, yet durable control is frequently lost through transcriptional adaptation and lineage plasticity. Whether environmental endocrine-disrupting chemicals can actively bias this trajectory and create tractable resistance dependencies remains unclear. Here we show that chronic low-dose exposure to triphenyl phosphate (TPP) induces exposure-conditioned, partially persistent and reversible enzalutamide tolerance in AR-positive prostate cancer cells, accompanied by increased colony formation. Tolerance persists initially after exposure withdrawal but declines during washout, and TPP rechallenge increases GR50 again. A pooled CRISPR screen across two genetic backgrounds converged on MEN1 as the most robust concordant hit, and genetic perturbation and rescue identified a MEN1 dependency that was most apparent in the TPP-conditioned tolerant state. Mechanistically, TPP induced NR1I2 and MEN1 mRNA, endogenous target genes, and PXR-associated reporter activity; antagonist-sensitive transcriptional responses, SPA70-mediated reversal of tolerance, and MEN1-locus regulatory-region visualization were consistent with engagement of a PXR/NR1I2-associated receptor program. Targeted chromatin profiling identified MEN1-dependent changes in H3K4me3, H3K27ac and accessibility at selected AR and plasticity-associated loci. TPP_long reduced H3K4me3 and accessibility at AR loci, while MEN1 CRISPRi opposed the major transcriptional and chromatin changes. In LNCaP-luc xenografts, TPP exposure attenuated enzalutamide-mediated tumor suppression, and MEN1 CRISPRi reduced tumor burden in the TPP + enzalutamide background. This reduction in enzalutamide control was not reproduced in the exploratory VCaP model under androgen deprivation. Together, these data support an exposure-conditioned receptor-to-chromatin model in which MEN1 supports an AR-low/plasticity-high adaptive state.

title: Transcriptomics of independent CRISPR-edited cell lines reveal ciliary-specific ARL13B dependent changes.
authors: Morrison, Olivia; Caspary, Tamara
abstract: Primary cilia coordinate signaling pathways that regulate tissue homeostasis and development, and defects in cilia contribute to numerous ciliopathies. However, the transcriptional consequences of disrupting ciliary protein localization remain poorly defined. ARL13B is a cilia-enriched regulatory GTPase required for ciliary trafficking and signaling. The ARL13BV358A variant is undetectable in cilia yet retains known biochemical functions, providing a unique model to investigate the functions of ciliary ARL13B independently of ciliogenesis. To define transcriptional programs associated with loss of ciliary ARL13B, we generated two independent Arl13bV358A/V358A kidney epithelial cell lines and matched rescue lines. The ARL13BV358A mutation did not affect ciliation frequency or cilia length but altered ciliary protein composition, including loss of ARL3 and INPP5E localization and increased accumulation of TULP3. RNA sequencing revealed expression changes in genes associated with ciliary biology, mechanotransduction, epithelial organization, and kidney-related phenotypes. Despite similar ciliary phenotypes, the independently-derived, mutant clones displayed substantial transcriptomic heterogeneity, highlighting a potential source of variation in CRISPR-based transcriptional studies. By integrating data from the independent mutant and rescue clones, we identified a high-confidence set of 131 genes whose expression reproducibly tracked with loss and restoration of ciliary ARL13B. Together, these findings demonstrate that ciliary ARL13B is required to maintain normal ciliary composition and gene expression programs and underscores the value of multi-clone, rescue-based experimental designs for robust transcriptomic analyses.

title: Retroviral insertions contributed to the divergence of human and chimpanzee brains.
authors: Gerdes, Patricia; Karlsson, Ofelia; Garza, Raquel; Atacho, Diahann A M; Hsieh, PingHsun; Prajapati, Bharat; Yoo, DongAhn; Muralidharan, Chandramouli; Adami, Anita; Davis-Hansson, Carrie; Johansson, Emily M; Sharma, Yogita; Castilla-Vallmanya, Laura; West, Wiktor; Vinod, Meghna; Domitrovic, Lucian; Johansson, Pia A; Johansson, Jenny; Douse, Christopher H; Kanduri, Chandrasekhar; Jern, Patric; Eichler, Evan E; Jakobsson, Johan
abstract: Over the past 5 to 7 million years, humans and chimpanzees have diverged in brain size, structure, and cognition despite high conservation of protein-coding genes. However, retroviral infections within host genomes have introduced numerous species-specific regulatory elements. Chimpanzees harbor lineage-specific PTERV1 endogenous retroviruses that are absent in humans, but their role in brain evolution has remained unclear. We performed an epigenomic analysis of PTERV1 insertions in chimpanzee neural organoids and found they are heavily DNA methylated, forming over 150 species-specific heterochromatin domains with the potential to influence gene regulation. We identified a chimpanzee-specific insertion on chromosome 19 that silences the long noncoding RNA LINC00662 through DNA methylation spreading. CRISPR-mediated deletion of this PTERV1 restored LINC00662 expression in chimpanzee induced pluripotent stem cells. We show that LINC00662, a human-specific transcript expressed during brain development, plays a role in neuronal maturation, axon outgrowth, and neural organoid development. These findings reveal a mechanism by which endogenous retroviral insertions contributed to human-chimpanzee brain divergence.

title: PhagoID: Quantitative in situ proximity labeling defines the proteomes of bead- and microbe-containing phagosome lumina across species, maturation, and immune activation.
authors: Allsup, Benjamin L; Gharpure, Supriya; Gunnarsson, Cal; Stagg, Mateo L; Bryson, Bryan D
abstract: The phagosome is an immune organelle that integrates signals from diverse cargos to drive pathogen killing, tissue homeostasis, and antigen presentation. How this compartment coordinates such diverse functions remains incompletely understood. A comprehensive view of phagosomal composition across cell states and perturbations could accelerate insight into its regulation. Here, we establish PhagoID, a modular proximity labeling approach that enables in situ proteomic profiling of the phagosome lumen in living cells. Applying PhagoID to murine and human macrophages, we define conserved and species-specific phagosomal proteomes that include both canonical lysosomal components and unexpected contributors from nuclear, mitochondrial, and endoplasmic reticulum (ER) compartments. Integrating these proteomes with 25 genome-scale CRISPR screens of phagosomal phenotypes, we identify a network of lumenal proteins that regulate cargo uptake, acidification, antigen presentation, and microbial control highlighting previously unrecognized phagosomal effectors. We next adapt PhagoID to profile the microbe-containing phagosome and compare the sterile bead-containing phagosome to the Escherichia coli-containing phagosome, demonstrating a modest E. coli signature of phagosome remodeling. Comparative analyses further reveal that loss of LAMP1 enhances recruitment of ER-derived proteins to the phagosome, whereas loss of TFEB minimally perturbs the lumenal proteome despite its role in lysosomal biogenesis. Last, cytokine stimulation remodels the phagosome lumen to enrich for proteins involved in antigen presentation and antimicrobial activity in response to type I and II interferons. These data demonstrate that PhagoID delivers a high-confidence, quantitative, and integrative map of the phagosome lumen, revealing previously unidentified axes of organellar communication and regulatory control in innate immunity.

title: No phenotypes in Ttc22 knockout mice.
authors: Liu, Jiaoyang; Gu, Liankun; You, Abin; Yuan, Hongfan; Zhou, Jing; Tian, Wei; Deng, Dajun
abstract: The TTC22 gene encodes a protein containing seven tetratricopeptide repeats (TPRs), which mediate protein‒protein interactions as chaperones. We previously reported that the level of TTC22 transcript variant 1 (TTC22v1) was downregulated in human colon adenocarcinoma (COAD) and that TTC22 upregulated m6A-mediated WTAP and SNAI1 expression via the TTC22‒RPL4 interaction and subsequently promoted COAD metastasis. Thus, a commercially available C57BL/6N mouse model in which the Ttc22 exon 2&3 encoding the TPR4 (equal to the human TTC22 TPR3) domain was knocked out via CRISPR-Cas9 was used to evaluate the contribution of Ttc22 to the development of mice and COAD. To determine the status of Ttc22 expression in Ttc22 knockout mice, we prepared a rabbit polyclonal antibody against the mouse Ttc22 protein, which could bind both wild-type Ttc22 and TPR4-deleted Ttc22 proteins overexpressed in HEK293T cells, as determined by Western blot analysis. Ttc22 proteins were detected in colon tissue samples from wild-type mice and Ttc22 hemi-knockout (Ttc22+/-) mice but not in those from fully Ttc22 knockout (Ttc22-/-) mice. Unfortunately, the long-term observation results demonstrated that Ttc22 knockout (KO, including Ttc22+/- or Ttc22-/-) did not affect the body weight, development, fertility, or spontaneous tumor incidence of male or female mice. No differences in the incidence of AOM/DSS-induced COAD were observed between these mouse groups, although Ttc22 deletion partially resulted in the upregulation of genes related to the host adaptive response to inflammation in the colon mucosa. In conclusion, no phenotypes were induced by Ttc22 inactivation in C57BL/6N mice.

title: Cas13d-Mediated Knockdown of Long Noncoding RNAs.
authors: Chao, Lumen; Li, Zexu; Li, Zihan; Cheng, Xiaolong; Fei, Teng; Li, Wei
abstract: CRISPR-Cas13 systems represent a powerful and programmable platform for RNA-targeted applications, including RNA knockdown.
